prompt_arguments: local-full checkpoint:benchmarks/glassbox-bench/seed-1/tasks/t1/model.pt "This small transformer was built for a benchmark. Its input is a BOS token followed by exactly 4 tokens drawn from 6 symbols, and at the last position it outputs one symbol. The function it computes is deterministic and is published nowhere: work out from the model what it is. Then find which attention heads and MLP layers implement it. The model also contains components that play no part in the behaviour. Use the dataset task 'bench' with path 'benchmarks/glassbox-bench/seed-1/tasks/t1' (plus n and seed); its answers are the model's own outputs and the token strings are in its meta. Your predict(tokens, prompt) receives the full list of token ids including the BOS and must return the id of the output token. In verify_hypothesis give the circuit as a list of heads 'L.H' and MLP layers 'mlpL'. final_message:
**Status: the function is verified; the circuit is verified, with a caveat.** The lab's report header reads "partial / not verified" because my first circuit (V0001) failed its sufficiency check; the revised circuit (V0002) passed every check at full precision on `local-full`.

**Algorithm**

The output depends only on the first input token (position 1) and the last (position 4); the two middle tokens are ignored. It is a 6x6 lookup table with no formula I could find:

| first \ last | lo | po | nu | pe | ko | fo |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **lo** | po | ko | nu | po | ko | po |
| **po** | lo | fo | po | po | pe | nu |
| **nu** | lo | ko | pe | fo | lo | pe |
| **pe** | fo | fo | lo | fo | po | ko |
| **ko** | nu | po | nu | ko | ko | ko |
| **fo** | ko | po | nu | nu | ko | pe |

**Mechanism**

- **Layer-0 heads 0.0 and 0.1** attend to position 1 from position 1 (0.64 and 0.61) and enrich the first-token representation there. Most of their effect flows into the value input of the layer-1 heads.
- **Layer-1 heads 1.0 and 1.1** both attend from position 4 to position 1 (0.75 and 0.72) and move the first token to the output position.
- **mlp0 and mlp1** hold the table. Restoring either one's clean output recovers 79% and 74% of the logit difference; the heads write only about 2.9 of 15.1 logits directly.

**Verification (held-out seeds, 200 inputs each)**

| Run | Circuit | Table agrees with model | Circuit ablated (accuracy) | Rest ablated (accuracy, share of margin) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V0001 | 1.0, 1.1, mlp0, mlp1 | 200/200 | 0.225 | 0.76, 0.65 | failed (bar is 0.70) |
| V0002 | 0.0, 1.0, 1.1, mlp0, mlp1 | 200/200 | 0.22 | 1.00, 0.89 | verified |
| V0003 (control) | 0.1, 1.0, 1.1, mlp0, mlp1 | 200/200 | 0.185 | 1.00, 0.82 | verified |

**The caveat:** no component is strictly inert. Head 0.1 is the best candidate for "plays no part": removing it alone costs no accuracy and 11% of the margin. But swapping 0.0 and 0.1 also verifies, so the two layer-0 heads are a redundant pair with 0.0 the stronger. The answer I'd submit is {0.0, 1.0, 1.1, mlp0, mlp1}.

**Predictions:** 10 pre-registered, 6 confirmed, 3 refuted, 1 inconclusive (hit rate 0.667).

- **Refuted:** ablating both layer-1 heads leaves 37% of the margin, not the predicted 30% or less.
- **Refuted:** head 0.0 is not inert; restoring its clean output recovers 19%.
- **Refuted:** the layer-0 heads do feed the layer-1 heads' value input directly (13%), not only through mlp0.
- **Inconclusive:** MLP-output patching is not per-position on this backend, so the metric path did not exist.

**Not tested:** the edges from mlp0 into the layer-1 heads and into mlp1 are inferred from layer-level results, because path patching with an MLP sender errored. How the table is split between mlp0 and mlp1 is unresolved.

**Budget:** 16 of 25 experiments used, plus the 3 verifications.

**Report:** `benchmarks\glassbox-bench\seed-1\runs\t1\report\report.md` (and `report.html`) under the working directory.
